title: Throughput-aware webhook batching with tenant rate-shaping and semantic dedup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers receive scheduled usage exports via S3 + webhook notifications. During spikes (large customers, bulk replay, or runaway retries) the webhook delivery fleet becomes overloaded: deliveries are delayed, retries increase, and SLOs for export latency and delivery success degrade. Current system uses a uniform retry/backoff per export manifest and a global dispatch queue with coarse tenant prioritization; it lacks a per-tenant shaping layer or semantic dedup that can collapse redundant delivery payloads.

Problem statement: We need a design and implementation that prevents noisy neighbors and runaway retries from impacting other tenants, reduces duplicate deliveries when manifests are updated repeatedly, and provides predictable SLAs for high-priority customers while remaining cost-efficient.

Goals (success criteria):
- Per-tenant concurrent webhook in-flight limit and token-bucket shaping enforceable across dispatcher workers.
- Semantic dedup of manifest notifications within a sliding window (configurable per customer) so repeated identical manifests collapse into a single delivery attempt.
- Backpressure signals from webhook clients (HTTP 429, TCP resets) cause tenant-level throttling and automatic retry escalation to S3-only fallback when sustained failures occur.
- Metrics and dashboards to surface per-tenant queue length, dedup hits, average end-to-end export latency, and retry amplification.
- Rollout with canary to 5% of tenants then gradated to 50% before full rollout.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Incoming delivery events (console trigger or export scheduler) produce a compact delivery envelope: {tenant_id, export_id, manifest_checksum, priority, route_preferences}. Envelopes are persisted in the delivery-log (append-only) and the dispatcher enqueues to a per-tenant logical queue implemented as: Redis streams + token bucket metadata in Redis for fast shaping.
2) Tenant shaping: token-bucket per tenant (tokens refill rate based on tier and configured concurrency). Dispatch workers atomically claim tokens before initiating HTTP webhook attempts. If no tokens, envelope is requeued with exponential jitter.
3) Semantic dedup: when a new envelope arrives, we compute a dedup key = sha256(tenant_id + manifest_checksum + route_preferences). Dedup entries live in a TTL'd Redis hash set keyed by tenant. If dedup key exists within window (default 30m), we increment a counter and attach referencing metadata to the existing envelope instead of enqueueing another delivery. When the first envelope completes (success/final failure), we attach the result to referencing customers and mark counters.
4) Failure/backoff policy: Transient HTTP 5xx or network timeouts => standard retry with increasing jitter. Client 4xx (except 429) => mark as final failure and route to admin-handled rerun. 429 or explicit backpressure header => escalate tenant token-bucket reduction and route lower-priority deliveries to S3-only notification path for N minutes. After sustained failures above threshold, automated CCR (customer-contact-remediation) event created for SRE to investigate.
5) S3-only fallback: For customers with frequent webhook failures, we keep their export artifacts in S3 and send a single administrative webhook telling them how to pick up pending manifests; this reduces webhook fleet load.
6) Observability: new metrics per tenant: in_flight_count, queue_depth, dedup_hit_rate, avg_delivery_latency, retry_multiplier, last_backoff_timestamp. Create Grafana dashboards and alerting rules for tenants exceeding configured thresholds.

Data and schema changes:
- delivery-log schema adds fields: dedup_key (string), token_claim_id (string), references (list of export ids serialized as CSV), shaping_tier (string), last_attempt_ts (ISO8601).
- Redis data structures: tenant:tokens:{tenant_id} (hash of tokens + refill_ts), tenant:dedup:{tenant_id} (TTL'd set of dedup keys).

Compatibility and migrations:
- New dispatcher will read existing delivery-log entries and process them unchanged. Migration steps: 1) deploy token-bucket and dedup feature flags off (read-only dedup store is ok); 2) enable dedup-write for a small test org; 3) enable shaping for 5% rollout; 4) slowly increase.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Dedup data and delivery metadata may contain PII-ish tenant identifiers. All keys stored in Redis are hashed (sha256(tenant_id||salt)) with salt rotated quarterly.
- S3 fallback paths must respect tenant encryption settings and pre-signed URL TTLs.
- security_review_required: true

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + integration against staging redis + simulated webhook endpoints (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for internal test tenants + 1 low-risk customer (1 week).
- Phase 2 (5% customers): enable shaping + dedup writes and observability (2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (50%): increase shaping aggressiveness for lower tiers; add S3-only fallback automation (2 weeks).
- Phase 4 (GA): global rollout + postmortem runbook (1 week).

Testing matrix:
- Dedup correctness: multiple identical manifest deliveries within window collapse into single attempt; referencing metadata correctly attached.
- Shaping effectiveness: simulate 10x traffic spike from a tenant and verify other tenants' latency unaffected.
- Backpressure response: simulate client 429/slow responses and assert token-bucket reduction and fallback routing.
- End-to-end: scheduled export -> manifest generation -> dedup + dispatch -> success/failure paths.

Open trade-offs and questions: 
- Where to store dedup reference lists for very large fanouts? Storing references in delivery-log row (DB) vs. Redis has cost and TTL trade-offs. Recommendation: keep small reference counts in Redis and overflow references to Postgres export_references table when > 50 references.
- Dedup window default (30m) chosen heuristically; some customers may want per-export-configurable windows. We should surface this as a per-tenant policy in Console (product work).
- Token-bucket parameters require calibration; suggest an initial conservative default that preserves P0 customer throughput while protecting P3.

Runbook and SRE actions:
- Dashboard alerts: tenant_queue_depth > 500, dedup_hit_rate > 80% and retries_per_min > 100 => throttle customers and contact success manager.
- Mitigations: increase token refill temporarily, move offending tenant to S3-only fallback, scale dispatcher workers, restart Redis replica if dedup set latency spikes.

Links and artifacts:
- design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/tenant-webhook-shaping-dedup
- draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/exports/pull/728 (WIP)
- load test harness: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/exports-loadtest/4321

Accept criteria:
- Core features implemented and feature-flagged behind tenant-webhook-shaping.
- Automated tests and load tests added to CI.
- Grafana dashboards and initial alerting in PagerDuty OR Slack channel.
- Successful canary with two customers and measurable reduction in cross-tenant interference.
